6. JavaScript — Module Logic

6.1 Minimal JS Skeleton

// mod-my_module.js
// Strict separation: no hardcoded text — everything via t()

const mmModule = (() => {

    // ── Helper functions ──────────────────────────────────────
    const $ = id => document.getElementById(id);

    function t(key) {
        const keys = key.split('.');
        let val = window.i18nData || {};
        for (const k of keys) {
            if (val && typeof val === 'object') val = val[k];
            else return key;
        }
        return typeof val === 'string' ? val : key;
    }

    function getCsrf() {
        return document.cookie.split(';')
            .map(c => c.trim())
            .find(c => c.startsWith('csrftoken='))
            ?.split('=')[1] || '';
    }

    // ── Initialization ──────────────────────────────────────
    function init() {
        console.log('My module initialized');
        loadData();
    }

    // ── Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────
    async function loadData() {
        try {
            const resp = await fetch('/api/my_module/data/');
            const data = await resp.json();
            renderData(data);
        } catch(e) {
            console.error('Error loading:', e);
        }
    }

    // ── Rendering ────────────────────────────────────────────
    function renderData(data) {
        const container = $('mm-container');
        if (!container) return;
        container.innerHTML = data.items.map(item => `
            <div class="mm-item">
                <strong>${item.name}</strong>
                <span>${item.value}</span>
            </div>
        `).join('');
    }

    // ── POST with CSRF ────────────────────────────────────────
    async function saveData(payload) {
        const resp = await fetch('/api/my_module/save/', {
            method:  'POST',
            headers: {
                'Content-Type': 'application/json',
                'X-CSRFToken':  getCsrf()
            },
            body: JSON.stringify(payload)
        });
        return await resp.json();
    }

    // ── Public API ──────────────────────────────────────
    return { init, loadData, saveData };

})();

// ── Events ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => mmModule.init());

document.addEventListener('languageChanged', e => {
    // On language change, reset UI texts
    console.log('Language changed:', e.detail.language);
    mmModule.init();
});

6.2 The t() Function — Translations

All texts in JS come from language files — never hardcode. The global variable window.i18nData contains all loaded translations:

// Simple key
t('my_module.title')           // → 'My Module'

// Nested key
t('my_module.errors.not_found') // → 'Not found'

// Key not found → key is returned
t('my_module.unknown')          // → 'my_module.unknown'

6.3 Using ABPE_CONFIG

// Available in every module JS:
const isAdmin = window.ABPE_CONFIG.is_admin;      // true/false
const lang    = window.ABPE_CONFIG.current_lang;  // 'de', 'en', ...
const apiUrl  = window.ABPE_CONFIG.api_url;       // '/api/'

// Example: Show admin section only for admins
if (window.ABPE_CONFIG.is_admin) {
    document.getElementById('admin-section').style.display = 'block';
}

6.4 languageChanged Event

When the user changes the language, core-language.js fires a custom event. The module JS can react to it:

document.addEventListener('languageChanged', function(e) {
    const newLang   = e.detail.language;   // 'en', 'fr', ...
    const moduleId  = e.detail.moduleId;   // 'my_module'

    // Update UI elements with new translations
    document.querySelectorAll('[data-i18n]').forEach(el => {

6.5 IIFE Pattern for Isolation

If a module JS could be loaded multiple times (e.g., through navigation without page reload), the IIFE pattern protects against duplicate declarations:

if (typeof window._mmModuleLoaded === 'undefined') {
    window._mmModuleLoaded = true;

    // ... entire module code here ...

}
